messages:
Priya K: Quick sync - during private endpoint testing we saw healthchecks flapping when control plane was in a different account + peered VPC. Looks like asymmetric return path + MTU fragmentation. Need agreement on guardrails and config we force on private endpoints.
Tom B: Can you paste an example trace? is it TCP conn reset or ICMP frag needed?
Evan L: Trace from the customer relay VM: SYN -> SYN-ACK -> client sends large TLS ClientHello (1400B) -> server responds with ACK then RST after fragmentation. Packet capture shows DF set and no PMTU discovery replies because egress NAT path drops ICMP.
Jin: Classic PMTU blackhole. Our relay side is behind a NAT gateway in their VPC for some accounts, and ICMP is blocked by their NACL. So MSS negotiation never reduces.
Maya S: That explains healthchecks failing for some customers at 1500 MTU. Our HTTP health probe does a GET with ~1KB headers (auth token) and TLS overhead pushes it over path MTU.
Priya K: Proposal: require endpoint onboarding checklist to include explicit MTU test and force TCP MSS clamping on our side for private endpoints when peer path indicates fragmentation issues. Options: 1) Recommend customer opens ICMP for PMTU; 2) We enable MSS clamp to 1380 for affected endpoints; 3) Provide QUIC-based probe fallback. Thoughts?
Tom B: 1 is ideal but often not possible with corporate firewalls. 3 is nice but a bigger engineering lift. MSS clamp + per-endpoint flag seems reasonable short-term.
Evan L: Agree. Implementation notes: clamp on the relay ENI's iptables PF_RULE so packets leaving to customer subnets get MSS 1380. We should also instrument a metric `endpoint_mtu_clamped` and tag it by tenant.
Jin: Another subtlety: asymmetric routing causes health check source IP to change if we SNAT on return path. We should preserve source IP for probes so customers can have stateless ACLs. Two options: 1) prefer route-based return path that preserves client source, 2) if SNAT required, advertise SNAT IP and include it in onboarding docs.
Maya S: From a product perspective, exposing a single `ingress_ip` for health checks (if we must SNAT) is useful. But preserve-source should be default for private endpoints - easier for customers.
Priya K: Agreed. Add to onboarding contract: default behavior = preserve source IP; if path requires SNAT, SE must enable `snat_mode` and we provide the SNAT IP to the customer before cutover. Also enforce a preflight that runs the following from a machine in their subnet:
```
# MTU probe
python3 -c "import socket,sys; s=socket.socket(); s.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1); s.connect(('10.0.1.5', 443)); print('connected')"
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null --max-time 2 "https://<private-endpoint>/healthz" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -w "%{http_code} %{size_request} %{size_download} %{time_total}s\n"
# Expect 200 and total bytes < path MTU allowance
```
Tom B: Minor nit: the python snippet doesn't craft large packets; better to use hping3 or tcpmss test. Example: `hping3 --syn -d 1400 -S -p 443 <endpoint>` to see if packet gets through.
Evan L: Also enforce route symmetry check: from customer subnet ping the relay ENI and traceroute back from relay to customer to validate return path uses peering (no internet detour). We can script that and fail preflight if hop count differs unusually.
Jin: For controller/CP separation: we should document that control plane traffic always uses peering route via private endpoints; control plane will abort handshake if route asymmetry detected for control-plane IPs. Handshake failure should return `ASYMMETRIC_ROUTE_DETECTED` before any heavy config sync. Less ambiguous than timeouts.
Maya S: Ops procedure if asymmetry discovered during onboarding: 1) Pause cutover, 2) provide remediation steps for customer (add route, allow ICMP, update NACL), 3) if customer can't change, offer SNAT-mode with noted limitations.
Priya K: For rollout: implement MSS clamp + metrics + per-tenant snat_mode toggle in the next sprint. Add a canary: enable clamp for 5 internal tenants for 48h, watch `healthcheck_success` and `endpoint_mtu_clamped`.
route-bot: route-change:peer-routing:update applied to tenant-beta (ops-123) :white_check_mark:
Tom B: Security note: if we preserve source IP, ensure we don't leak internal IPs into logs for hosted control plane. Mask logged source IPs for hosted model or anonymize in dashboards.
Evan L: Good catch. We'll add a `source_ip_masked` flag in observability when endpoint.private=true and controlplane_hosted=true. That is an internal display change only.
Priya K: I'll write up the onboarding checklist and the fallback modes (preserve-source, snat-mode, quic-probe fallback) and share for review. Aim to lock behavior by EOD Friday. Thanks all.
